   354	# Citation-resolution scan for one file. Matches both `(path:L##[-L##])`
   355	# and bare table-cell `path:L##` with a single regex — the surrounding
   356	# parens/pipes are not part of the match, so one pass covers both forms.
   357	_validate_translation_citations() {
   358	    local f="$1" in_fence=false lineno=0 line
   359	    # Held in a single-quoted variable (never a bare literal in a =~/== RHS)
   360	    # so the parser never treats the backticks as command substitution.
   361	    local fence='```'
   362	    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
   363	        lineno=$((lineno + 1))
   364	
   365	        if [[ "$line" == "$fence"* || "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]+${fence} ]]; then
   366	            [[ "$in_fence" == true ]] && in_fence=false || in_fence=true
   367	            continue
   368	        fi
   369	        [[ "$in_fence" == true ]] && continue
   370	
   371	        # markdown-link / bare-URL forms — skip wholesale to avoid false
   372	        # positives (a URL's "domain.tld/path:L##"-shaped substring is not
   373	        # a citation into this repo).
   374	        [[ "$line" == *'](http'* || "$line" == *'://'* ]] && continue
   375	
   376	        # R2 review (cycle-120): the incremental `while [[ =~ ]]` scan below is
   377	        # superlinear on a single very long path-dense line (LLM translation
   378	        # docs routinely carry wide tables / pasted logs on one unwrapped line),
   379	        # which would hang this MUST gate with no output. Cap line length; a
   380	        # citation the gate must resolve never needs 2000+ chars on one line.
   381	        # WARN rather than silently skip so an over-long line is visible.
   382	        if (( ${#line} > 2000 )); then
   383	            warnings+=("line ${lineno} exceeds 2000 chars — citation scan skipped for this line (wrap long tables/logs)")
   384	            continue
   385	        fi
   386	
   387	        local rest="$line"
   388	        while [[ "$rest" =~ ([A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,6}):L([0-9]+)(-L[0-9]+)? ]]; do
   389	            local cited_path="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
   390	            local cited_startline="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
   391	            local match_full="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"
   392	            rest="${rest#*"$match_full"}"
   393	
   394	            # {...}-placeholder citations (e.g. `{file}:L{N}`) never reach
   395	            # here — the regex requires a real dotted extension and real
   396	            # digits — but guard explicitly in case a brace rides along a
   397	            # real-looking path.
   398	            [[ "$cited_path" == *'{'* || "$cited_path" == *'}'* ]] && continue
   399	
   400	            local resolved="" base
   401	            for base in "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa" "$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa/reality"; do
   402	                if [[ -f "$base/$cited_path" ]]; then
   403	                    resolved="$base/$cited_path"
   404	                    break
   405	                fi
   406	            done
   407	
   408	            if [[ -z "$resolved" ]]; then
   409	                violations+=("CITATION UNRESOLVED: '$cited_path:L$cited_startline' cited at $f:$lineno does not resolve under repo-root, grimoires/loa/, or grimoires/loa/reality/ — fix the path or remove the citation")
   410	                continue
   411	            fi
   412	
   413	            local total_lines
   414	            total_lines=$(wc -l < "$resolved" | tr -d ' ')
   415	            if [[ "$total_lines" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( cited_startline > total_lines )); then
   416	                violations+=("CITATION LINE OUT OF RANGE: '$cited_path:L$cited_startline' cited at $f:$lineno but $resolved has only $total_lines lines — fix the cited line number")
   417	            fi
   418	        done
   419	    done < "$f"
   420	}

   354	# Citation-resolution scan for one file. Matches both `(path:L##[-L##])`
   355	# and bare table-cell `path:L##` with a single regex — the surrounding
   356	# parens/pipes are not part of the match, so one pass covers both forms.
   357	_validate_translation_citations() {
   358	    local f="$1" in_fence=false lineno=0 line
   359	    # Held in a single-quoted variable (never a bare literal in a =~/== RHS)
   360	    # so the parser never treats the backticks as command substitution.
   361	    local fence='```'
   362	    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
   363	        lineno=$((lineno + 1))
   364	
   365	        if [[ "$line" == "$fence"* || "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]+${fence} ]]; then
   366	            [[ "$in_fence" == true ]] && in_fence=false || in_fence=true
   367	            continue
   368	        fi
   369	        [[ "$in_fence" == true ]] && continue
   370	
   371	        # markdown-link / bare-URL forms — skip wholesale to avoid false
   372	        # positives (a URL's "domain.tld/path:L##"-shaped substring is not
   373	        # a citation into this repo).
   374	        [[ "$line" == *'](http'* || "$line" == *'://'* ]] && continue
   375	
   376	        # R2 review (cycle-120): the incremental `while [[ =~ ]]` scan below is
   377	        # superlinear on a single very long path-dense line (LLM translation
   378	        # docs routinely carry wide tables / pasted logs on one unwrapped line),
   379	        # which would hang this MUST gate with no output. Cap line length; a
   380	        # citation the gate must resolve never needs 2000+ chars on one line.
   381	        # WARN rather than silently skip so an over-long line is visible.
   382	        if (( ${#line} > 2000 )); then
   383	            warnings+=("line ${lineno} exceeds 2000 chars — citation scan skipped for this line (wrap long tables/logs)")
   384	            continue
   385	        fi
   386	
   387	        local rest="$line"
   388	        while [[ "$rest" =~ ([A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,6}):L([0-9]+)(-L[0-9]+)? ]]; do
   389	            local cited_path="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
   390	            local cited_startline="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
   391	            local match_full="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"
   392	            rest="${rest#*"$match_full"}"
   393	
   394	            # {...}-placeholder citations (e.g. `{file}:L{N}`) never reach
   395	            # here — the regex requires a real dotted extension and real
   396	            # digits — but guard explicitly in case a brace rides along a
   397	            # real-looking path.
   398	            [[ "$cited_path" == *'{'* || "$cited_path" == *'}'* ]] && continue
   399	
   400	            local resolved="" base
   401	            for base in "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa" "$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa/reality"; do
   402	                if [[ -f "$base/$cited_path" ]]; then
   403	                    resolved="$base/$cited_path"
   404	                    break
   405	                fi
   406	            done
   407	
   408	            if [[ -z "$resolved" ]]; then
   409	                violations+=("CITATION UNRESOLVED: '$cited_path:L$cited_startline' cited at $f:$lineno does not resolve under repo-root, grimoires/loa/, or grimoires/loa/reality/ — fix the path or remove the citation")
   410	                continue
   411	            fi
   412	
   413	            local total_lines
   414	            total_lines=$(wc -l < "$resolved" | tr -d ' ')
   415	            if [[ "$total_lines" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( cited_startline > total_lines )); then
   416	                violations+=("CITATION LINE OUT OF RANGE: '$cited_path:L$cited_startline' cited at $f:$lineno but $resolved has only $total_lines lines — fix the cited line number")
   417	            fi
   418	        done
   419	    done < "$f"
   420	}

   736	# Lines of $FILE outside fenced code, inline code spans removed, prefixed "NR<TAB>".
   737	_prd_prose_lines() {
   738	    awk '
   739	        /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }
   740	        fence { next }
   741	        { line = $0; gsub(/`[^`]*`/, "", line); printf "%d\t%s\n", NR, line }
   742	    ' "$FILE"
   743	}

   745	validate_prd_assumptions() {
   746	    local prose
   747	    prose="$(_prd_prose_lines)"
   748	    local n_fact n_dec n_bare
   749	    n_fact=$(grep -oE '\[ASSUMPTION fact\]' <<< "$prose" | wc -l | tr -d ' ' || true)
   750	    n_dec=$(grep -oE '\[ASSUMPTION decision\]' <<< "$prose" | wc -l | tr -d ' ' || true)
   751	    n_bare=$(grep -oE '\[ASSUMPTION\]' <<< "$prose" | wc -l | tr -d ' ' || true)
   752	    info_lines+=("[ASSUMPTION] tags: $(( ${n_fact:-0} + ${n_dec:-0} + ${n_bare:-0} ))")
   753	    info_lines+=("assumption tag classes: fact=${n_fact:-0} decision=${n_dec:-0} bare=${n_bare:-0}")
   754	
   755	    local prd_date
   756	    prd_date="$(grep -m1 -E '^\*\*Date:?\*\*:?' -- "$FILE" | grep -oE '[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}' | head -1 || true)"
   757	    if [[ "${n_bare:-0}" -gt 0 ]]; then
   758	        if [[ -n "$prd_date" && ! "$prd_date" < "$BARE_ASSUMPTION_FAILS_FROM" ]]; then
   759	            violations+=("${n_bare} bare [ASSUMPTION] tag(s): a PRD dated ${prd_date} (on or after ${BARE_ASSUMPTION_FAILS_FROM}) must name the class, [ASSUMPTION fact] or [ASSUMPTION decision] (DEC-NNNN)")
   760	        else
   761	            warnings+=("${n_bare} bare [ASSUMPTION] tag(s): name the class, [ASSUMPTION fact] or [ASSUMPTION decision] (DEC-NNNN); bare tags fail for PRDs dated from ${BARE_ASSUMPTION_FAILS_FROM}")
   762	        fi
   763	    fi
   764	
   765	    local tagged deferred
   766	    tagged="$(grep -E $'^[0-9]+\t.*\\[ASSUMPTION decision\\]' <<< "$prose" || true)"
   767	    deferred="$(grep -E $'^[0-9]+\t[[:space:]]*([-*][[:space:]]+)?\\*\\*Deferred:?\\*\\*:?' <<< "$prose" || true)"
   768	    [[ -n "$tagged" || -n "$deferred" ]] || return 0
   769	
   770	    local unattended=false
   771	    if _dec_context_why --prd "$FILE" | grep -q '^unattended'; then unattended=true; fi
   772	
   773	    local ledger="${LEDGER_FILE:-${PROJECT_ROOT}/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml}" rows=""

   775	        rows="$(yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$ledger" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '(.decisions // [])[] | objects | "\(.id)\t\(.source // "")"' 2>/dev/null || true)"

   782	        [[ -n "$ln" ]] || continue
   783	        ids="$(grep -oE 'DEC-[0-9]{4,}' <<< "$text" || true)"
   784	        ok=false

   787	            if awk -F'\t' -v id="$id" -v n="$prd_name" '$1 == id && index($2, n) > 0 { f = 1 } END { exit !f }' <<< "$rows"; then ok=true; break; fi

   790	    done <<< "$tagged"

   792	        [[ -n "$ln" ]] || continue
   793	        ids="$(grep -oE 'DEC-[0-9]{4,}' <<< "$text" || true)"
   794	        ok=false
   795	        while IFS= read -r id; do
   796	            [[ -n "$id" ]] || continue

   811	# The PRD is the sibling prd.md of the sprint file. A requirement is deferred when its

+
+In `rounds` pacing, a round is one message even when `discovery_questions` is `structured`: present the numbered round as markdown and take the reply as text, because a round can hold more questions than one AskUserQuestion call allows.
+
+## Question Pacing
+
+One key, `interview.pacing`, sets the pacing for the discovery interview, `/architect` Phase 2, `/sprint-plan` Phase 2 and `/chart`. Those skills point here.
+
+| Pacing | Behavior |
+|---|---|
+| `sequential` | Ask ONE question per turn. Wait for response. Then ask the next. The supported opt-out from rounds. |
+| `batch` | Present 3-6 numbered questions. User responds to all at once. The `minimal` default. |
+| `rounds` | Ask the whole frontier per turn, as below. The `thorough` default. |
+
+### Rounds
+
+1. **Frontier.** The frontier is every open question whose prerequisites are settled. A question that depends on another question still open waits for a later round. There is no cap on round size.
+2. **Facts stay out.** A fact (what code, reality files or docs say) is looked up, never asked; only decisions enter a round (Backpressure Protocol, "Fact or decision").
+3. **Phase scope.** A round runs within the current discovery phase. A question that belongs to a later phase is parked for that phase. Phase gates are unchanged.
+4. **Format.** Number questions across the session (`Q1`, `Q2`, ...), so ids never restart. Each question has a short title line starting `❓ Q<n>:`, the question worded so that "yes" accepts the recommendation, and a `➡ Recommended:` line giving the answer and its reason, with a citation when there is one. Close the round with the answer prompt and the comment block.
+5. **Answers.** A bare "yes" accepts every recommendation in the round. A numbered answer (`2: no, keep it local`) overrides that question. If the operator answers some numbers and not others, restate the unanswered ones with their recommendations and ask for confirmation; they take the recommendation only after the operator confirms. A question still unconfirmed is re-asked in the next round.
+6. **Recompute.** Before the next round, recompute the frontier from the answers: settled questions leave, questions whose prerequisites just settled join. "wrap up" ends the phase.
+7. **Comment block.** End every round with one HTML comment holding a JSON array, one object per question: `{"id": "Q4", "depends_on": ["Q1"]}`. `depends_on` lists the earlier questions this one needed settled, `[]` when none. A re-asked question keeps its id and carries `"reasked": true`. The block is how `tools/check-round-independence.sh` checks that no question in a round depends on another question in the same round.

+❓ Q5: Unattended record
+Should unattended runs write a DEC row for every decision they take for you?
+➡ Recommended: yes (makes "which did a human decide?" answerable)
+

     6	# `disable-model-invocation: true`. The harness refuses those to the Skill
     7	# tool (tests/unit/user-invoked-harness.bats), so no other command or skill
     8	# body may tell the model to run one as a step. Asserts:
     9	#   1. every listed command file exists and carries the flag
    10	#   2. no other body has an operative line for a listed name
    11	#   3. every command file carrying the flag is listed

    13	#      or context --clear (those are reachable only through /decisions)
    14	# Each check is a function over a root directory, proved against fixtures.

    17	    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    18	    export LC_ALL=C
    19	}

    21	# list_names <root>: the allowlisted names, comments and blanks stripped
    22	list_names() {
    23	    sed -e 's/#.*$//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//' -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' \
    24	        "$1/.claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt" | grep -v '^$' || true

    27	# frontmatter <file>: the first YAML frontmatter block (empty when none)

    29	    awk 'NR==1 && $0!="---"{exit} /^---[[:space:]]*$/{n++; if(n==2) exit; next} n==1{print}' "$1"
    30	}
    31	
    32	has_flag() {
    33	    frontmatter "$1" | grep -Eq '^disable-model-invocation:[[:space:]]*"?true"?[[:space:]]*$'
    34	}
    35	
    36	# check_listed_flagged <root>: prints each listed name whose file is missing or unflagged
    37	check_listed_flagged() {
    38	    local root="$1" name f
    39	    while IFS= read -r name; do
    40	        f="$root/.claude/commands/$name.md"
    41	        if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then
    42	            echo "missing: $name"
    43	        elif ! has_flag "$f"; then
    44	            echo "unflagged: $name"
    45	        fi
    46	    done < <(list_names "$root")
    47	}
    48	
    49	# check_flagged_listed <root>: prints each flagged command file not in the list

    54	        [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
    55	        has_flag "$f" || continue
    56	        name="$(basename "$f" .md)"
    57	        grep -qxF "$name" <<<"$names" || echo "unlisted: $name"
    58	    done
    59	}

    61	# check_operative <root>: prints file:line for each operative reference to a
    62	# listed name in a body other than that command's own file
    63	check_operative() {
    64	    local root="$1" name re exempt
    65	    exempt='(^|[^[:alpha:]])(user|operator|human|manually|suggest|recommend|tell|ask)'
    66	    while IFS= read -r name; do
    67	        # SDD D-8.3 pattern, widened: verbs match in any case and may take
    68	        # "the" ("execute /x", "Invoke the /x skill").
    69	        re="([Ee][Xx][Ee][Cc][Uu][Tt][Ee]|[Ii][Nn][Vv][Oo][Kk][Ee]|[Rr][Uu][Nn]|[Cc][Aa][Ll][Ll])[[:space:]]+(the[[:space:]]+)?\`?/${name}([^[:alnum:]_-]|\$)|Skill\\(.*${name}"

    71	          find "$root/.claude/skills" -name '*.md' -type f 2>/dev/null; } |

    73	            [[ "$f" == "$root/.claude/commands/$name.md" ]] && continue

    78	}

    81	# an operator-only dec-write-lib.sh operation
    82	check_operator_ops() {

    85	        frontmatter "$f" | awk '/^allowed-tools:/{on=1; print; next} on && /^[[:space:]]+-|^[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]/{print; next} {on=0}' |

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# user-invoked-harness.bats: does `disable-model-invocation: true` hide a
     4	# command from the model's Skill tool? (FR-8, SDD D-8.4)
     5	# =============================================================================
     6	# One live `claude -p` run in a throwaway project holding two fixture commands:
     7	# `fixture-hidden` (flagged) and `fixture-visible` (control, unflagged). The
     8	# live run gets the Skill tool only, so it cannot read the fixture bodies or
     9	# run anything else, and it never sees a real Loa command.
    10	#
    11	# Outcomes of the live test:
    12	#   pass   the control ran (its marker reached the stream) and the hidden
    13	#          command did not (no Skill tool_use for it, or an error result,
    14	#          and its marker is absent everywhere)
    15	#   fail   the hidden marker reached the stream: the flag does not hide the
    16	#          command, so FR-8 is lint-only and G-7 partial
    17	#   skip   no `claude` on PATH; LOA_HARNESS_CHECK=0; CLI error, timeout or
    18	#          unparsable output; or the control never ran (inconclusive)
    19	# Set LOA_HARNESS_OUT=<file> to keep the raw stream-json as evidence.
    20	# The classifier is also exercised offline against canned streams.
    21	
    22	HIDDEN_MARK="HIDDEN-RAN"
    23	VISIBLE_MARK="VISIBLE-RAN"
    24	
    25	# classify_stream <stream-json file>
    26	# Prints one of: verified | flag-does-not-hide | inconclusive-control | unparsable
    27	classify_stream() {
    28	    local stream="$1"
    29	    if ! jq -e -s 'length > 0' "$stream" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    30	        echo "unparsable"
    31	        return 0
    32	    fi
    33	    # Marker text anywhere in a tool result, an injected user message or the
    34	    # final result means that command's body was loaded into the session.
    35	    local hidden_seen visible_seen
    36	    hidden_seen="$(jq -r -s --arg m "$HIDDEN_MARK" \
    37	        '[.[] | select(.type == "user" or .type == "result" or .type == "assistant") | tostring | contains($m)] | any' "$stream")"
    38	    visible_seen="$(jq -r -s --arg m "$VISIBLE_MARK" \
    39	        '[.[] | select(.type == "user" or .type == "result" or .type == "assistant") | tostring | contains($m)] | any' "$stream")"
    40	    if [[ "$hidden_seen" == "true" ]]; then
    41	        echo "flag-does-not-hide"
    42	    elif [[ "$visible_seen" != "true" ]]; then
    43	        echo "inconclusive-control"
    44	    else
    45	        echo "verified"
    46	    fi
    47	}
    48	
    49	# skill_calls <stream-json file>: one line per Skill tool_use, "<name>\t<is_error>"
    50	skill_calls() {
    51	    jq -r -s '
    52	      ([.[] | select(.type == "user") | .message.content[]? | select(.type? == "tool_result")
    53	         | {key: .tool_use_id, value: ((.is_error // false) | tostring)}] | from_entries) as $res
    54	      | .[] | select(.type == "assistant") | .message.content[]?
    55	      | select(.type? == "tool_use" and .name == "Skill")
    56	      | "\(.input.skill // .input.command // .input.name // "?")\t\($res[.id] // "no-result")"' "$1"
    57	}
    58	
    59	write_fixture_project() {
    60	    local dir="$1"
    61	    mkdir -p "$dir/.claude/commands"
    62	    git -C "$dir" init -q
    63	    cat > "$dir/.claude/commands/fixture-hidden.md" <<'EOF'
    64	---
    65	name: fixture-hidden
    66	description: fixture
    67	disable-model-invocation: true
    68	---
    69	
    70	Reply with the single word HIDDEN-RAN
    71	EOF
    72	    cat > "$dir/.claude/commands/fixture-visible.md" <<'EOF'
    73	---
    74	name: fixture-visible
    75	description: fixture
    76	---
    77	
    78	Reply with the single word VISIBLE-RAN
    79	EOF
    80	}

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# user-invoked-harness.bats: does `disable-model-invocation: true` hide a
     4	# command from the model's Skill tool? (FR-8, SDD D-8.4)
     5	# =============================================================================
     6	# One live `claude -p` run in a throwaway project holding two fixture commands:
     7	# `fixture-hidden` (flagged) and `fixture-visible` (control, unflagged). The
     8	# live run gets the Skill tool only, so it cannot read the fixture bodies or
     9	# run anything else, and it never sees a real Loa command.
    10	#
    11	# Outcomes of the live test:
    12	#   pass   the control ran (its marker reached the stream) and the hidden
    13	#          command did not (no Skill tool_use for it, or an error result,
    14	#          and its marker is absent everywhere)
    15	#   fail   the hidden marker reached the stream: the flag does not hide the
    16	#          command, so FR-8 is lint-only and G-7 partial
    17	#   skip   no `claude` on PATH; LOA_HARNESS_CHECK=0; CLI error, timeout or
    18	#          unparsable output; or the control never ran (inconclusive)
    19	# Set LOA_HARNESS_OUT=<file> to keep the raw stream-json as evidence.
    20	# The classifier is also exercised offline against canned streams.
    21	
    22	HIDDEN_MARK="HIDDEN-RAN"
    23	VISIBLE_MARK="VISIBLE-RAN"
    24	
    25	# classify_stream <stream-json file>
    26	# Prints one of: verified | flag-does-not-hide | inconclusive-control | unparsable
    27	classify_stream() {
    28	    local stream="$1"
    29	    if ! jq -e -s 'length > 0' "$stream" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    30	        echo "unparsable"
    31	        return 0
    32	    fi
    33	    # Marker text anywhere in a tool result, an injected user message or the
    34	    # final result means that command's body was loaded into the session.
    35	    local hidden_seen visible_seen
    36	    hidden_seen="$(jq -r -s --arg m "$HIDDEN_MARK" \
    37	        '[.[] | select(.type == "user" or .type == "result" or .type == "assistant") | tostring | contains($m)] | any' "$stream")"
    38	    visible_seen="$(jq -r -s --arg m "$VISIBLE_MARK" \
    39	        '[.[] | select(.type == "user" or .type == "result" or .type == "assistant") | tostring | contains($m)] | any' "$stream")"
    40	    if [[ "$hidden_seen" == "true" ]]; then
    41	        echo "flag-does-not-hide"
    42	    elif [[ "$visible_seen" != "true" ]]; then
    43	        echo "inconclusive-control"
    44	    else
    45	        echo "verified"
    46	    fi
    47	}
    48	
    49	# skill_calls <stream-json file>: one line per Skill tool_use, "<name>\t<is_error>"
    50	skill_calls() {
    51	    jq -r -s '
    52	      ([.[] | select(.type == "user") | .message.content[]? | select(.type? == "tool_result")
    53	         | {key: .tool_use_id, value: ((.is_error // false) | tostring)}] | from_entries) as $res
    54	      | .[] | select(.type == "assistant") | .message.content[]?
    55	      | select(.type? == "tool_use" and .name == "Skill")
    56	      | "\(.input.skill // .input.command // .input.name // "?")\t\($res[.id] // "no-result")"' "$1"
    57	}
    58	
    59	write_fixture_project() {
    60	    local dir="$1"
    61	    mkdir -p "$dir/.claude/commands"
    62	    git -C "$dir" init -q
    63	    cat > "$dir/.claude/commands/fixture-hidden.md" <<'EOF'
    64	---
    65	name: fixture-hidden
    66	description: fixture
    67	disable-model-invocation: true
    68	---
    69	
    70	Reply with the single word HIDDEN-RAN
    71	EOF
    72	    cat > "$dir/.claude/commands/fixture-visible.md" <<'EOF'
    73	---
    74	name: fixture-visible
    75	description: fixture
    76	---
    77	
    78	Reply with the single word VISIBLE-RAN
    79	EOF
    80	}

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# dec-write-lib.bats: the decision-ledger writer (.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh).
#
# Hermetic: every test copies the writer, its validator and compat-lib into a fresh temp project
# (its own git repo and .run), so the host's run state, the live ledger and the operator's session
# never leak in. The live grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml of this repository is never written.
# Seams: the CLI (subcommands, exit codes) and the ledger file after each operation.
# =============================================================================

# An empty ledger carrying the tracked file's header only: fixtures never inherit live rows
# (the live ledger is seeded in the main checkout).
empty_ledger(){ { sed '/^schema_version:/,$d' "$1"; printf 'schema_version: 1\ndecisions: []\n'; } > "$2"; }

setup() {
  BATS_TEST_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not installed"
  command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not installed"
  [[ "$(yq --version 2>&1)" == *mikefarah*"version v4."* ]] || skip "Mike Farah yq v4 not installed"
  unset CLAUDE_SESSION_ID CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID LOA_UNATTENDED LOA_FLATLINE_MODE CI GITHUB_ACTIONS \
        LOA_HOOK_CONTEXT LOA_DEC_NO_FLOCK LOA_DEC_LOCK_WAIT
  T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/proj"
  mkdir -p "$T/.claude/scripts/lib" "$T/grimoires/loa"
  cp "$REPO/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh" "$T/.claude/scripts/lib/"
  cp "$REPO/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh" "$REPO/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh" "$T/.claude/scripts/"
  [[ -f "$REPO/.claude/scripts/pii-filter.sh" ]] && cp "$REPO/.claude/scripts/pii-filter.sh" "$T/.claude/scripts/"
  empty_ledger "$REPO/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml" "$T/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml"
  git -C "$T" init -q
  D="$T/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh"
  L="$T/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml"
  F="$T/fixture.yaml"
  cp "$L" "$F"
  ALT='{"option":"keep sequential","rejected_because":"one question per turn is slow"}'
}

# Same transformation as the writer's san1() (kf-write-lib.sh's), used to state expected values.
DEC_ULB_RE="$(printf '\302[\200-\237]|\342\200[\250\251]')"
san1(){ printf '%s' "${1-}" | LC_ALL=C tr -d '\000-\010\013\014\016-\037\177' | LC_ALL=C tr '\t\n\r' '   ' | LC_ALL=C sed -E "s/${DEC_ULB_RE}/ /g"' ; s/  +/ /g; s/^ //; s/ $//'; }

# new_open FILE [extra args]  -> an open row
new_open(){ local f="$1"; shift; bash "$D" new --file "$f" --summary "an open question" --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by plan-and-analyze --source "prd.md#fr-1" --quiet "$@"; }
# new_prop FILE [extra args]  -> a proposed row
new_prop(){ local f="$1"; shift; bash "$D" new --file "$f" --summary "rounds is the thorough default" --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by plan-and-analyze --source "prd.md#e (D1)" --status proposed --decision "pacing rounds" --rationale "brief recommendation" --alternative-json "$ALT" --cycle cycle-128 --quiet "$@"; }
field(){ yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$1" | jq -r --arg id "$2" ".decisions[] | select(.id == \$id) | $3"; }
ids(){ yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$1" | jq -r '[.decisions[].id] | join(",")'; }
confirm_op(){ bash "$D" confirm --recorded-by decisions-command --evidence "cli:2026-10-13T12:00:00Z" --quiet "$@"; }
lockpath(){ # target -> the writer's lock path
  local abs; abs="$(cd "$(dirname "$1")" && pwd -P)/$(basename "$1")"
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  ( source "$REPO/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; printf '%s/.run/.dec-write-%s.lock' "$(cd "$T" && pwd -P)" "$(printf '%s' "$abs" | sha256_portable | cut -c1-12)" )
}
# A PATH holding every command of the current PATH except $1 (the tool reads as absent).
path_without(){
  local tool="$1" d="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/pw-$1" p f b
  mkdir -p "$d"
  local IFS=:

# =============================================================================
# dec-write-lib.bats: the decision-ledger writer (.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh).
#
# Hermetic: every test copies the writer, its validator and compat-lib into a fresh temp project
# (its own git repo and .run), so the host's run state, the live ledger and the operator's session
# never leak in. The live grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml of this repository is never written.
# Seams: the CLI (subcommands, exit codes) and the ledger file after each operation.

# An empty ledger carrying the tracked file's header only: fixtures never inherit live rows
# (the live ledger is seeded in the main checkout).
empty_ledger(){ { sed '/^schema_version:/,$d' "$1"; printf 'schema_version: 1\ndecisions: []\n'; } > "$2"; }

setup() {
  BATS_TEST_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not installed"
  command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not installed"

  unset CLAUDE_SESSION_ID CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID LOA_UNATTENDED LOA_FLATLINE_MODE CI GITHUB_ACTIONS \
        LOA_HOOK_CONTEXT LOA_DEC_NO_FLOCK LOA_DEC_LOCK_WAIT
  T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/proj"
  mkdir -p "$T/.claude/scripts/lib" "$T/grimoires/loa"
  cp "$REPO/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh" "$T/.claude/scripts/lib/"
  cp "$REPO/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh" "$REPO/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh" "$T/.claude/scripts/"
  [[ -f "$REPO/.claude/scripts/pii-filter.sh" ]] && cp "$REPO/.claude/scripts/pii-filter.sh" "$T/.claude/scripts/"
  empty_ledger "$REPO/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml" "$T/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml"
  git -C "$T" init -q
  D="$T/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh"
  L="$T/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml"

# Same transformation as the writer's san1() (kf-write-lib.sh's), used to state expected values.
DEC_ULB_RE="$(printf '\302[\200-\237]|\342\200[\250\251]')"
san1(){ printf '%s' "${1-}" | LC_ALL=C tr -d '\000-\010\013\014\016-\037\177' | LC_ALL=C tr '\t\n\r' '   ' | LC_ALL=C sed -E "s/${DEC_ULB_RE}/ /g"' ; s/  +/ /g; s/^ //; s/ $//'; }

# new_open FILE [extra args]  -> an open row
new_open(){ local f="$1"; shift; bash "$D" new --file "$f" --summary "an open question" --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by plan-and-analyze --source "prd.md#fr-1" --quiet "$@"; }
# new_prop FILE [extra args]  -> a proposed row
new_prop(){ local f="$1"; shift; bash "$D" new --file "$f" --summary "rounds is the thorough default" --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by plan-and-analyze --source "prd.md#e (D1)" --status proposed --decision "pacing rounds" --rationale "brief recommendation" --alternative-json "$ALT" --cycle cycle-128 --quiet "$@"; }
field(){ yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$1" | jq -r --arg id "$2" ".decisions[] | select(.id == \$id) | $3"; }
ids(){ yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$1" | jq -r '[.decisions[].id] | join(",")'; }
confirm_op(){ bash "$D" confirm --recorded-by decisions-command --evidence "cli:2026-10-13T12:00:00Z" --quiet "$@"; }
lockpath(){ # target -> the writer's lock path
  local abs; abs="$(cd "$(dirname "$1")" && pwd -P)/$(basename "$1")"
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  ( source "$REPO/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; printf '%s/.run/.dec-write-%s.lock' "$(cd "$T" && pwd -P)" "$(printf '%s' "$abs" | sha256_portable | cut -c1-12)" )
}
# A PATH holding every command of the current PATH except $1 (the tool reads as absent).
path_without(){
  local tool="$1" d="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/pw-$1" p f b
  mkdir -p "$d"
  local IFS=:
  for p in $PATH; do
    [[ -d "$p" ]] || continue

  done
  printf '%s' "$d"
}

head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:359 — The "operator-only" gate for confirm, reject or supersede on a decided row, and `context --clear` is just the string `--recorded-by decisions-command`, and any agent with Bash can pass it. I reproduced it: `LOA_UNATTENDED= dec-write-lib.sh confirm --id DEC-0004 --recorded-by decisions-command --evidence cli:… --answer-ref cli:…` moved an agent-proposed row to `decided` with `decided_by: operator`. So the central claim (decisions.md:25-26, "an agent that could run them would confirm its own decisions") is not enforced. The writer needs a check the model cannot forge (for example a TTY/interactive operator confirmation or a deny rule in settings.json), or the docs must stop presenting this as a guarantee.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:642 — `import` copies every pending row into the live ledger unchanged, including its status, decided_by and transitions. Nothing checks that an imported row is still `open`/`proposed` with a single null->open|proposed transition and `decided_by: null`. The validator never limits new rows either; validate-artifact.sh:686 rejects them only while a live unattended signal holds. I reproduced it: a hand-written decisions-pending.yaml row with `status: decided`, `decided_by: operator` and an `operator:decisions-command` transition imported as DEC-0003 `decided`/`operator`, rc=0. A worktree agent can therefore skip /decisions confirm entirely.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:580 — Rejecting a supersede proposal (agent supersede, then reject of the new row) leaves `supersede_proposed_by` on the old decided row pointing at the rejected row. After that the agent path refuses every later supersede of that row ("a replacement is already proposed", line 601). The validator also forbids clearing the field (validate-artifact.sh:681 allows the change only from null). Reproduced: after supersede DEC-0001 -> DEC-0002 and reject DEC-0002, a new `supersede --id DEC-0001` exits 1. Reject should clear the back-pointer on the superseded row in the same write, and the append-only rule should allow that.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:667 — `list` treats a missing ledger as empty and exits 0. head/.claude/skills/run-mode/resources/render-templates.md:104 — `jq -r '.active_cycle'` prints the literal `null` when there is no active cycle (or ledger.json lacks the key). `list --cycle null` then matches no rows and exits 0, so the PR body reports "every decision in this run was the operator's" when agent rows exist. Any `bats tests/unit` run on a machine with `claude` on PATH therefore makes a real, billed, networked `claude -p` call that can take up to 180 s. head/.claude/hooks/session-start/loa-decisions-surface.sh:79 — `IFS=$'\t' read` treats TAB as IFS whitespace, so adjacent tabs collapse. A row whose id is missing or sanitises to "" (line 75) shifts its fields: the status lands in the id slot and the summary in the status slot. Emit a placeholder id (for example `?`) or use a non-whitespace delimiter.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:718 — `context --clear` removes only `${PROJECT_ROOT}/.run/unattended.json`, but `ctx_signals` (line 166) also reads the main checkout's `.run` from a linked worktree. In a worktree, `/decisions clear-unattended` therefore reports success while the main checkout's marker keeps the context unattended.
head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:787 — The tag-to-row rule accepts a DEC row when `index(source, basename(PRD)) > 0`, a plain substring test. Any source containing `prd.md` satisfies it (for example `sub-prd.md`, `old/prd.md.bak`, or another directory's prd.md), so an `[ASSUMPTION decision]` can cite a row recorded for a different PRD. Match the source's path component instead.
head/.claude/commands/decisions.md:27 — The text says `tests/unit/dec-write-lib.bats` checks that no other command or skill calls these operations. The tests at dec-write-lib.bats:548/558 and user-invoked-commands.bats:86 only grep SKILL.md allowed-tools and the literal `--recorded-by decisions-command`. A body that runs `dec-write-lib.sh confirm` (or passes the recorder through a variable) in prose or in a non-SKILL resource is not caught. The test coverage is overstated.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

content.text:
The verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**: the PR's main promise, that only the operator can confirm a decision, isn't enforced. The review is in `/workspace/review.md`: 11 findings, one per line, ending with `Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED`.

I couldn't run the PR's bats suites because the frozen tree doesn't include the libraries they load. Instead, the first four findings below I reproduced by running the PR's `dec-write-lib.sh` and validator in a scratch project with a minimal stand-in for `compat-lib.sh`. The rest come from reading the code.

**Blocking defects:**
- **An agent can confirm its own decisions.** The "operator-only" check is just the flag `--recorded-by decisions-command`, which any agent with shell access can pass. Unsetting the unattended environment variable on the same line gets past the unattended check too. Hiding `/decisions` from the model (`disable-model-invocation`) doesn't stop it calling the script directly. In my run, an agent-proposed row went to `decided` with `decided_by: operator`.
- **Importing from a worktree skips confirmation.** `import` copies rows from the pending file as they are. A hand-edited pending file with a row already marked `decided` by the operator was accepted into the ledger.
- **A rejected replacement blocks the old row for good.** When a proposed replacement is rejected, the old row keeps pointing at it. After that, every agent attempt to propose a new replacement is refused, and the validator doesn't allow the pointer to be cleared.
- **A missing ledger looks like "the operator decided everything".** `list` treats a missing ledger as empty and succeeds, printing "_None: every decision in this run was the operator's._" Separately, the PR-body steps in `render-templates.md` read the cycle with `jq -r '.active_cycle'`. When no cycle is set, that yields the literal `null`, which matches no rows and produces the same false message.
- **The unit tests spend money by default.** A new test makes a real, billed `claude -p` call whenever `claude` is installed, unless `LOA_HARNESS_CHECK=0` is set. It should be opt-in.

**Lower-severity issues:**
- The validator check for deferred requirements uses a pattern (`#{1,3}`) that the default awk on Debian/Ubuntu (mawk 1.3.4-20200120) doesn't support. I confirmed it never matches, so tasks get false warnings.
- In the session-start hook, a row with an empty id shifts its columns, because consecutive tabs collapse when the line is split.
- `/decisions clear-unattended` run in a worktree doesn't clear the main checkout's marker, so the session stays unattended.
- The check that a PRD's `[ASSUMPTION decision]` tags cite matching ledger rows only does a substring match on the PRD's filename, so a row recorded for a different PRD can satisfy it.
- `decisions.md` says the tests check that no other command or skill calls the operator-only operations; they only check part of that.

- **The unit tests spend money by default.** A new test makes a real, billed `claude -p` call whenever `claude` is installed, unless `LOA_HARNESS_CHECK=0` is set. It should be opt-in.

**Lower-severity issues:**
- The validator check for deferred requirements uses a pattern (`#{1,3}`) that the default awk on Debian/Ubuntu (mawk 1.3.4-20200120) doesn't support. I confirmed it never matches, so tasks get false warnings.
- In the session-start hook, a row with an empty id shifts its columns, because consecutive tabs collapse when the line is split.
- `/decisions clear-unattended` run in a worktree doesn't clear the main checkout's marker, so the session stays unattended.
- The check that a PRD's `[ASSUMPTION decision]` tags cite matching ledger rows only does a substring match on the PRD's filename, so a row recorded for a different PRD can satisfy it.
- `decisions.md` says the tests check that no other command or skill calls the operator-only operations; they only check part of that.
